content: Have you ever wondered why some families get bigger or move to new places? Nimmi is very excited today! A new member has arrived in her house. Her mother has given birth to a cute little baby girl. The whole house is filled with joy.

Socratic Question: If a new baby comes to your house right now, how would your daily life change? Who will take care of the baby? Where will the baby sleep? What new things will your family have to buy?

content.title: A Growing Family Tree
content.description: Watch how the family tree adds a new branch when a baby is born.

content: When a new baby is born, they become a new member of the family. The baby is called an infant. If the baby is your brother or sister, they are your sibling. The size of the family increases, and everyone shares new responsibilities to care for the baby. Families are always changing and growing!

definition: A very young child or baby.

question: What happens to the size of a family when a new baby is born?

content: Reflection: Think about your own family. Have you ever had a new baby cousin or sibling born? How did your daily routine change to help take care of them? Explain it to your younger sibling or a friend.

Connection to Biology: Just like human families grow when babies are born, animal families also grow. Animals have babies too! Think about how a puppy joins a family of dogs. Knowledge is connected across different subjects!

Students often think a family only changes when someone is born. Remember, families also change when someone gets married (like a new aunt or uncle joining) or when a family member transfers to a new city for a job!

Mastery Challenge: Draw your own family tree on a piece of paper. Start with your grandparents at the top, then your parents and uncles/aunts, and finally you, your siblings, and your cousins at the bottom. Circle the newest member of your family!

Tsering's father has received a letter from his office. The letter says that he is being promoted and will have to move to another city! Meanwhile, in Nazli's house, there is great joy because her elder cousin brother is getting married. How do these events change their families?
Can you predict what happens when someone gets married? Does a new person join the family, or does someone leave? What happens when a family member gets transferred to a new city?

content.title: Moving and Joining
content.description: Visualizing two houses: one person moving far away, and another person joining a new house.

content: When a family member gets married, a new person (like a bride or groom) joins the family. The family size increases and new relationships are formed. On the other hand, when someone is transferred to a new city for work, they might have to leave their joint family and start living as a nuclear family in the new place.

definition: A large family where grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, and cousins all live together in the same house.
A smaller family consisting only of parents and their children.

question: What happens to the structure of a family when a member gets transferred to a new city?
options: They might move and form a nuclear family
They always stop talking to their relatives

content: Reflection: Imagine you have to move to a new city because of your parents' job transfer. What things would you miss the most about your old house and friends? What new things would you be excited to discover?
Geography Connection: When people move to new cities, they might experience different weather, eat different food, and even hear a new language! Moving teaches us how to adapt to new environments.

Mastery Challenge: Interview your parents or grandparents. Ask them where they lived when they were your age. Did they ever move to a new place or live in a joint family? Write down their story in your notebook!
